tasks.short: Complete employee timesheets from recorded arrivals, departures and approved corrections.

steps.what: Retrieve arrival and departure records from the {HCM}.
Check missing punches, overlapping entries and differences against scheduled hours.
Ask employees to correct incomplete entries before the payroll cutoff.
Enter corrected times and explain deviations in the {HCM}.
Approve corrected times and payable overtime.
Transfer approved hours and pay codes into the {PAYROLL}.

tasks.design: Configure exception checks, correction forms and approval reminders in the {HCM}. A validated connector transfers approved hours into the {PAYROLL}, with duplicate protection, control totals and an import report; employees supply missing facts and managers approve corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: The basic features already exist. Inconsistent pay codes, disconnected records and unfinished approval setup often leave clerks chasing corrections.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration and AI-assisted connector development make local mappings and checks cheaper to implement. No model is needed to calculate hours.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed hours, overnight shifts, collective agreement provisions and late corrections still need reliable facts and accountable decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Employees explain what happened; managers judge disputed attendance and authorise payable exceptions.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of unresolved time entries before payroll cutoff.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time copying hours and sending reminders. With delegated authority, they can prioritise manager escalations each day; approval of disputed hours remains with managers.

reach.task: Resolve recurring absence-code errors affecting pay.
reach.learn: Absence categories, collective agreement provisions and the boundary between attendance facts and medical information.

evidence.claim: Attendance checks, approval routing and hours transfers can use existing configuration and deterministic rules.
In the Netherlands, employee-data and attendance-monitoring arrangements can require works-council consent under article 27.
The digest documents a Dutch fine for fingerprint attendance registration; biometric clocking is not a default solution.
GDPR applies to attendance data. Consultation duties and monitoring safeguards require assessment under applicable national rules.

assumptions: The typical employer records attendance in a time module within the {HCM}; paper records may remain for exceptions.
Time shares describe the whole workflow, including employee corrections and manager approval.
The target transfers approved attendance facts and does not infer employee performance.
Build ranges cover one employing entity and one payroll interface; consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which attendance features and interfaces the customer's {HCM} supports.
The actual mix of electronic, document and paper time records.
Applicable jurisdictions, collective agreements and employee consultation requirements.
Who may approve overtime and corrections after cutoff.
research_questions: Can existing configuration cover shift boundaries, breaks and overtime without custom calculations?
Which recurring exceptions arise from bad source data rather than missing rules?
Does the proposed change trigger a GDPR impact assessment or consultation under national rules?
new_work: Review failed imports and unresolved time exceptions.
Maintain pay code mappings, calendars and escalation routes.
Test shift and agreement changes before they affect payroll.
Monitor access, retention and approval logs.

tasks.short: Answer employee and manager questions about pay, tax, benefits and collective agreement provisions.

steps.what: Receive and log the payroll question.
Check relevant employee records, payslips and recorded pay changes.
Find applicable policy, benefit and collective agreement passages.

loop.input: The question and approved documents filtered by jurisdiction, employee group and effective date.
loop.output: Relevant quoted passages with document versions, dates and locations.
loop.check: Verify every quotation against its source; the clerk checks applicability and conflicting provisions.
loop.stop: One retrieval pass and one retry within ten passages; missing or conflicting sources go to a specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions and provisions use different wording; keyword search alone often misses the relevant passage.

steps.what: Resolve the case interpretation or consult the responsible specialist.
Draft a clear answer with supporting figures and policy references.

loop.input: The question, checked payroll facts, cited passages and the clerk's answer basis.
loop.output: A plain-language draft with traceable figures, references and any unresolved question.
loop.check: Match figures to source fields and citations to approved passages; reject unsupported eligibility or tax conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unresolved claims return to the clerk without sending.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard questions, but varied questions need tailored explanations across several sources.

steps.what: Discuss sensitive, disputed or confusing pay issues with the employee.
Approve the answer, send it to authorised recipients and record closure.

tasks.design: A restricted inquiry queue in the {HELPDESK} gathers authorised facts from the {HCM} and {PAYROLL}. Bounded retrieval and drafting loops use approved documents in the {DOCS}; the clerk resolves interpretation, handles sensitive conversations and approves each reply before the {EMAIL} sends it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers depend on employee-specific records and several changing documents. A searchable library alone does not establish which provision applies.
tasks.enabler_now: Read-only connectors can assemble facts, while bounded models can retrieve passages and draft explanations with source checks. These capabilities reduce preparation without transferring interpretation rights.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting provisions, personal tax circumstances, disputed entitlement and distress about pay require specialist judgement and careful conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk understands the concern behind a question, explains uncertainty and knows when to involve a specialist.

ambition.what: Pre-payday pay-change explanations for employees with variable pay.

tasks.altitude: The clerk's week shifts toward difficult cases and clearer explanations. Delegated routine-answer authority may expand, while benefit exceptions and legal interpretations remain with the responsible specialists.

reach.task: Explain how a benefit eligibility rule affects an employee's pay.
reach.learn: Plan eligibility, effective dates, source precedence and escalation boundaries.
Agreement coverage, interpretation records and when a formal dispute process applies.

evidence.claim: Restricted fact retrieval and cited drafting are feasible patterns, but the digest supplies no documented payroll inquiry case.
A bounded model can help explain payroll warnings, provided the clerk checks the explanation against records.
GDPR access controls and data minimisation apply to employee-specific answers; EU AI Act duties depend on intended use.

assumptions: Questions usually arrive through the {EMAIL}, with calls for sensitive cases.
Published policies and collective agreements have identifiable owners and effective dates.
The target explains recorded pay and approved rules; it does not decide employee eligibility or performance.
Time shares average routine inquiries and the smaller set requiring conversation.
unknowns: Whether the customer has a suitable restricted queue in the {HELPDESK}.
Which employee and manager identities can access each payroll field.
Which questions the clerk may answer without specialist approval.
Whether approved model processing arrangements cover the relevant employee data.
Which national rules or employee consultation duties apply.
research_questions: Which inquiry categories can use fixed templates without a model?
Can effective dates and agreement coverage be filtered reliably before retrieval?
How often do source documents conflict or omit the answer?
Can a pilot measure unsupported claims and handling time using anonymised historical questions?
new_work: Review draft answers and source applicability.
Maintain policy versions, approved explanations and escalation routes.
Handle failed retrieval, uncertain identity and conflicting records.
Sample answers for unsupported claims and excess disclosure.
Maintain model instructions and regression examples after policy changes.

tasks.short: Verify employment facts and provide authorised statements to requesting third parties.

steps.what: Receive and log an employment verification request.
Verify requester identity, disclosure basis and permitted information.
Check employment dates, job details and any authorised earnings information.
Populate the approved employment statement template.
Check the draft for incorrect facts and excess disclosure.
Authorise and send the employment statement to the verified recipient.

tasks.design: A request form in the {WORKFLOW} records identity evidence, permitted fields and the verified recipient. Deterministic lookups from the {HCM} and {PAYROLL} populate a controlled template in the {DOCS}; an authorised signatory approves the exact statement and recipient before the {EMAIL} sends it and records disclosure.
tasks.previous_blocker: Low request volumes, varied requester forms and uncertainty about disclosure authority made manual handling appear sufficient.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, field allowlists and document templates already cover most of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of connecting records and generating consistent statements.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticating unusual requests, reconciling historical records and deciding whether a requested disclosure is lawful remain case-specific.
tasks.human_edge: A person recognises suspicious requests and protects the employee when requested information exceeds the legitimate purpose.

ambition.what: Tracked self-service requests for standard employment letters.

tasks.altitude: The clerk handles identity and record exceptions instead of repeatedly typing letters. Routine release authority can be delegated explicitly, but automation grants no new disclosure rights.

reach.task: Produce standard employment-status letters from employee records.
reach.learn: Permitted fields, historical employment records, identity checks and retention rules.

evidence.claim: Structured employment facts can populate controlled templates without a model.
GDPR requires a lawful disclosure basis, appropriate security and data minimisation; employee consent is not automatically the correct basis.
The digest contains no documented employment-verification automation case.

assumptions: This task means responding to requests about current or former employees, rather than checking candidates' references.
Standard statements contain factual employment information and exclude recommendations or predictions.
Earnings information is included only where the verified purpose and disclosure basis permit it.
Nonstandard requester forms remain exceptions unless a controlled mapping is worthwhile.
unknowns: Whether the customer's verification work concerns outgoing statements or candidate background checks.
Who holds release authority and whether electronic signatures are required.
Which requester types, jurisdictions and statement formats occur.
Whether historical records are complete and accessible.
The customer's disclosure bases, retention periods and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: What proportion of requests fit one controlled factual template?
Which identity checks can be configured without weakening assurance?
Can the {HCM} generate the required statement directly?
Which conflicting historical fields must stop generation?
new_work: Review requester identity and disclosure exceptions.
Maintain templates, field allowlists and signatory permissions.
Check delivery failures and maintain disclosure records.

tasks.short: Prepare, reconcile, approve and submit payroll tax returns.

steps.what: Retrieve approved payroll totals and filing-period details.
Reconcile payroll tax totals with liability accounts in the {ERP}.
Investigate differences and enter supported payroll corrections.
Generate the payroll tax return from corrected payroll records.
Review validation results, approve the return and submit it.
Check acceptance and archive the return, receipt and reconciliation.

tasks.design: Use maintained statutory filing features in the {PAYROLL}, with a deterministic reconciliation to liability accounts in the {ERP}. The payroll lead approves the exact return before submission through the supported {PAYROLL} connection or {GOV_PORTAL}; responses, exceptions and evidence are recorded in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Return generation is often already automated. Manual work persists around ledger reconciliation, correction evidence, approval handoffs and acceptance tracking.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing filing functions can be configured, while small connectors can reconcile totals and collect receipts. Faster implementation helps join these functions without building a new tax calculation engine.
tasks.still_hard: Cross-border treatment, retroactive corrections, legislative changes and rejected returns need payroll or tax expertise.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk distinguishes timing differences from errors, and the payroll lead accepts responsibility for corrections and filing.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of emerging payroll tax reconciliation differences.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving differences before filing week. With delegated authority, they can close documented timing differences; tax-treatment corrections and return release retain their approvers.

reach.task: Check payroll tax treatment of a new benefit before launch.
reach.learn: Taxable benefit categories, effective dates, supporting evidence and specialist escalation.

reach.task: Assess payroll readiness for employees working across jurisdictions.
reach.learn: Registration requirements, responsibility boundaries and when tax advice is needed.

evidence.claim: In the Netherlands, employers with more than ten staff file payroll tax returns using commercial software and the prescribed electronic channel.
Nmbrs Payroll provides salary-change run checks; this supports configurable checking, not proof that a return is legally correct.
Nmbrs Payroll provides employee-level comparisons across three payroll periods.
Ledger reconciliation, duplicate-submission prevention and receipt tracking can use deterministic controls.
The digest provides no documented payroll filing automation case with measured savings.

assumptions: The employer or its payroll provider uses maintained statutory filing features in the {PAYROLL}.
A workbook commonly bridges payroll totals and liability accounts where a direct reconciliation is absent.
The target covers one jurisdiction and one employing entity initially.
A correction invalidates any prior approval of the affected return.
Employee consultation under national rules is assessed where the change alters employee-data arrangements; filing automation alone does not establish that requirement.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, entities and filing frequencies apply.
Whether the customer or an external payroll provider submits returns.
Which submission and acceptance interfaces are supported.
The actual reconciliation process and frequency of retroactive corrections.
Who may approve corrections and release returns.
Which access grants and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can the {PAYROLL} already reconcile the relevant liabilities without a custom connector?
Which differences can be classified using exact documented rules?
How does the filing channel distinguish receipt from acceptance?
How are rejected, corrected and superseded returns linked without duplicate submission?
new_work: Review unmatched liabilities and correction evidence.
Maintain account mappings, filing calendars and access credentials.
Test reconciliation controls after statutory or interface changes.
Handle rejected submissions and verify acceptance.
Review access logs and evidence retention.

role.altitude: The role shifts from copying records and chasing handoffs toward resolving payroll exceptions and explaining pay. Any additional decision rights require explicit delegation; disputed hours, sensitive disclosures, tax interpretation and filing release keep named approvers.
reach: Human resources specialists: resolve recurring employee-record and absence-code problems before payroll cutoff.
Compensation and benefits specialists: check how benefit changes flow into pay and tax treatment.
Labor relations specialists: identify collective agreement questions requiring formal interpretation.
Human resources assistants: operate controlled employee-letter and payroll-inquiry services.
skills_to_grow: Payroll control totals, reconciliations and exception diagnosis.
Effective-dated pay codes, policy rules and collective agreement coverage.
Access control, GDPR data minimisation and national consultation requirements.
Clear explanations of pay and sensitive employee conversations.
Connector specifications, approval controls and configuration testing.
Checking model drafts against authoritative records and current sources.
role.ambitious_version: A payroll operations specialist who detects upstream errors earlier, offers approved pre-payday explanations and runs reliable employee services. Deterministic controls handle routine records; bounded models prepare cited explanations; people retain consequential judgement and release authority.
